elements.quote: We searched all English information sources from 1 December 2019 to 4 March 2022, and the Chinese literature from conception of the databases to 20 February 2021.
elements.reason: The text explicitly reports the search dates for English and Chinese information sources.

elements.quote: The database includes, but is not limited to the following: 25 bibliographic and grey literature sources: Medline (Ovid and PubMed), PubMed Central, Embase, CAB Abstracts, Global Health, PsycInfo, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Academic Search Complete, Africa Wide Information, CINAHL, ProQuest Central, SciFinder, the Virtual Health Library, LitCovid, WHO covid-19 website, CDC covid-19 website, Eurosurveillance, China CDC Weekly, Homeland Security Digital Library, ClinicalTrials.gov, bioRxiv (preprints), medRxiv (preprints), chemRxiv (preprints), and SSRN (preprints).
elements.reason: Names and interfaces of databases are reported, but available coverage dates for each database are not explicitly detailed.

elements.quote: ClinicalTrials.gov, bioRxiv (preprints), medRxiv (preprints), chemRxiv (preprints), and SSRN (preprints). We stopped searching the Chinese databases on 20 February 2021
elements.reason: Names of registers and repositories are listed, and search date restrictions are reported.

elements.quote: WHO covid-19 website, CDC covid-19 website... MAGIC Evidence Ecosystem Foundation (www.magicevidence.org)
elements.reason: Names of websites are reported, but URLs are not provided for all sources (e.g., WHO, CDC).

elements.quote: These included the Living Overview of the Evidence (L-OVE) COVID-19 Repository by the Epistemonikos Foundation and the Systematic and Living Map on COVID-19 Evidence by the Norwegian Institute of Public Health, in collaboration with the Cochrane Canada Centre at McMaster University.
elements.reason: Organisations providing information sources are named.
No information is provided regarding types of individuals contacted to identify studies.
No information is provided regarding the types of reference lists examined.
No information is provided regarding backward or forward citation searching.
No information is provided regarding journals or conference proceedings consulted.

elements.quote: The supplementary file includes the WHO literature search strategy, which is maintained and tested on an ongoing basis by two WHO research librarians and one US CDC research librarian. ... The supplementary file includes the Chinese literature search strategy.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states that the full search strategies for WHO and Chinese literature are included in the supplementary file.

elements.quote: We searched all English information sources from 1 December 2019 to 4 March 2022, and the Chinese literature from conception of the databases to 20 February 2021.
elements.reason: Search limits (dates, languages) are described, but explicit justification by reference to eligibility criteria is not provided in the text.

elements.quote: We adapted the search terms for covid-19 developed by the CDC to the Chinese language.
elements.reason: A published search approach (CDC) is cited, and the adaptation to Chinese language is described.

elements.quote: To identify randomised trials, we filtered the results through RobotSearch, a validated and highly sensitive machine learning model.
elements.reason: RobotSearch, a text-analysis/machine learning tool, is specified for filtering results.
No specific tools used to translate search strings between sources are specified in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The supplementary file includes the WHO literature search strategy, which is maintained and tested on an ongoing basis by two WHO research librarians and one US CDC research librarian.
elements.reason: Testing/maintenance by librarians is mentioned, but specific validation studies or detailed validation process are not described.
No peer review of the search strategy (e.g., PRESS) is described in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Randomised trials in which people at risk of covid-19 were allocated to prophylaxis or no prophylaxis (standard care or placebo).
elements.reason: The search structure appears to be based on PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome), so this conditional element does not apply.

elements.quote: pairs of reviewers independently screened all titles and abstracts, followed by full texts of trials that were identified as potentially eligible.
elements.reason: The text explicitly states that pairs of reviewers screened titles, abstracts, and full texts.

elements.quote: pairs of reviewers independently screened all titles and abstracts
elements.reason: The text explicitly states that reviewers screened independently.

elements.quote: A third reviewer adjudicated conflicts.
elements.reason: The text describes the process for resolving disagreements via a third reviewer.
No information is provided regarding processes to obtain or confirm eligibility information from study investigators.
No information is provided regarding methods used to translate abstracts or full articles.

elements.reason: The text mentions the use of Covidence software for the review process.
No information is provided regarding externally derived classifiers.
No information is provided regarding internally derived classifiers.

elements.reason: Explicitly states that pairs (two) of reviewers performed data extraction.

elements.quote: pairs of reviewers extracted data independently
elements.reason: Explicitly states that reviewers worked independently during data extraction.

elements.quote: Reviewers resolved discrepancies by discussion and, when necessary, with adjudication by a third party.
elements.reason: Describes the process for resolving disagreements between data collectors.
No information regarding processes to obtain or confirm data from study investigators is reported in the retrieved evidence.
While Covidence is mentioned for screening, no automation tools for data collection/extraction are described in the retrieved evidence.
Methods used to translate articles are not described in the retrieved evidence.
Software used to extract data from figures is not specified in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Because of inconsistent reporting across trials, when possible, we preferentially extracted participant characteristics and outcome data for participants with a polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test that was negative for SARS-CoV-2 infection at baseline. If authors did not report data separately for those who were PCR-negative for SARS-CoV-2 infection at baseline, we extracted data from all participants, regardless of their PCR status at baseline.
elements.reason: Describes decision rules for selecting data when reporting is inconsistent across trials.

elements.quote: Reviewers collected information on trial characteristics (trial registration, publication status, study status, design), participant characteristics (country, age, sex, comorbidities), exposure characteristics (exposure status, exposureduration,highriskgroup)andoutcomesofinterest(means or medians and measures of variability for continuous outcomes and the number of participants analysed and the number of participants who experienced an event for dichotomous outcomes).
elements.reason: The text explicitly lists and defines the variables sought, including trial, participant, exposure, and outcome characteristics.

elements.quote: If authors did not report data separately for those who were PCR-negative for SARS-CoV-2 infection at baseline, we extracted data from all participants, regardless of their PCR status at baseline.
elements.reason: The text describes the assumption and procedure applied when specific data regarding PCR status was missing or unclear.

elements.quote: using a standardised, pilot tested data extraction form
elements.reason: A data extraction form is mentioned as a tool, but no specific tool name or citation is provided in the text.

elements.quote: used a revision of the Cochrane tool for assessing risk of bias in randomised trials (RoB 2.0)
elements.reason: The specific tool (Cochrane RoB 2.0) and version are explicitly specified.

elements.quote: across the following domains: bias arising from the randomisation process; bias owing to departures from the intended intervention; bias from missing outcome data; bias in measurement of the outcome; bias in selection of the reported results, including deviations from the registered protocol; bias due to competing risks; and bias arising from early termination for benefit.
elements.reason: All domains assessed by the risk-of-bias tool are explicitly listed.

elements.quote: We rated trials at high risk of bias overall if one or more domains were rated as probably high risk of bias or as high risk of bias and as low risk of bias if all domains were rated as probably low risk of bias or low risk of bias.
elements.reason: The overall risk-of-bias judgement and the rules for deriving it are clearly reported.

elements.quote: used a revision of the Cochrane tool
elements.reason: The text explicitly states that a 'revision' or 'modification' of the existing tool was used.
No newly developed risk-of-bias tool was used; an existing tool (RoB 2.0) was modified.

elements.quote: Reviewers resolved discrepancies by discussion and, when not possible, with adjudication by a third party.
elements.reason: Disagreement resolution procedures are reported, but the specific number of reviewers for risk of bias assessment is not explicitly stated (unlike the GRADE assessment where 'Two methodologists' is mentioned).
No description of processes used to obtain or confirm risk-of-bias information from study investigators is found.
No description of automation tools used for risk-of-bias assessment is found.

elements.quote: We summarised the effect of prophylactic drugs on laboratory confirmed infection and on laboratory confirmed, suspected, and probable infection using odds ratios (ORs) and corresponding 95% credible intervals (CrIs). Due to low number of events in most studies, we summarised all other dichotomous outcomes using risk differences (RDs) and corresponding 95% credible intervals (CrIs).
elements.reason: The text explicitly specifies odds ratios for infection outcomes and risk differences for other dichotomous outcomes.

elements.quote: Pending data from quantitative studies of patient values, we chose thresholds of small but important effects of 0.1% for mortality; 2% for adverse events leading to discontinuation and laboratory confirmed infection; 3% for suspected, probable, or laboratory confirmed infection; and 1% for admission to hospital.
elements.reason: Thresholds for interpreting effect size (small but important effects) are reported along with their rationale.

elements.quote: To facilitate interpretation of the results, we calculated absolute effects for laboratory confirmed infection and suspected, probable, and laboratory confirmed infection-outcomes that were summarised as ORs.
elements.reason: The text describes the method used to re-express relative effects (ORs) into absolute effects for interpretation.

elements.quote: Due to low number of events in most studies, we summarised all other dichotomous outcomes using risk differences (RDs) and corresponding 95% credible intervals (CrIs).
elements.reason: The choice of risk differences is explicitly justified by the low number of events in most studies.

elements.quote: Weexcluded randomised trials published only as press releases and trials that evaluated vaccination, nutrition, and non-drug supportive care interventions. We synthesised randomised trials that evaluated drugs, and antibody and cellular therapies for treatment of covid-19 in separate living network meta-analyses.
elements.reason: The text explicitly describes the process of excluding specific interventions and separating trials into different syntheses (prophylaxis vs treatment), thereby defining eligibility for each synthesis.

elements.quote: Because of inconsistent reporting across trials, when possible, we preferentially extracted participant characteristics and outcome data for participants with a polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test that was negative for SARS-CoV-2 infection at baseline. If authors did not report data separately for those who were PCR-negative for SARS-CoV-2 infection at baseline, we extracted data from all participants, regardless of their PCR status at baseline.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes a specific method for handling inconsistent reporting during data extraction (preferentially extracting PCR-negative data, otherwise all participants), which constitutes a method required to prepare data for synthesis.

elements.quote: We created GRADE evidence summaries (Summary of Findings tables), developed in the MAGIC Authoring and Publication Platform (www.magicapp.org), to provide userfriendly formats for clinicians and patients, and allow re-use in the context of clinical practice guidelines for covid-19, such as the WHO living guidelines.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes the tabular structure used (Summary of Findings tables) and the data included (outcomes such as laboratory confirmed infection, admission to hospital, and mortality).

elements.quote: We used the networkplot command of Stata version 15.1 (StataCorp, College Station, TX) to create network plots in which the inverse variance of the direct comparison was proportional to the thickness of lines between nodes and the number of participants randomised to the intervention was proportional to the size of nodes.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the graphical methods used (network plots) and the specific visual encoding (line thickness, node size) in detail.

elements.quote: We categorised the interventions from the most to the least effective using the minimally contextualised GRADE guidance to drawing conclusions from NMAs, which considers the effect estimates and the certainty of the evidence.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports a basis for ordering interventions (most to least effective) in the interpretation of results, but does not explicitly describe the ordering of individual studies within tables or graphs.
The manuscript describes standard network and forest plots without mentioning the use of non-standard graphs, so the rationale for non-standard graphs is not applicable.

elements.quote: using the R package gemtc 21... We performed analyses in RStudio version 3.5.3 (R Studio, Boston, MA, USA).
elements.reason: Software package (gemtc 21) and version (RStudio 3.5.3) are explicitly reported.

elements.quote: different prophylactic drugs were assessed precluding meta-analysis. Further, neither trial met the sample size criteria for network meta-analysis.
elements.reason: Identifies that meta-analysis was not possible but does not describe the alternative synthesis or summary method used.

elements.quote: we performed random effects network meta-analysis
elements.reason: Model (random effects network meta-analysis) and rationale (comparative effectiveness) are reported.

elements.quote: random effects network meta-analysis using the R package gemtc 21 andusedthree Markov chains with 100 000 iterations
elements.reason: Statistical method (random effects NMA, Markov chains) is reported.

elements.quote: Node splitting models provided methods to obtain indirect estimates and to assess local heterogeneity.
elements.reason: Methods to assess heterogeneity (Node splitting models) are reported.

elements.quote: Wechoseanon-informativepriorforthevarianceparameter
elements.reason: Between-study variance handling (informative prior) is reported in the Bayesian context.

elements.quote: 95% credible interval (CrI) 2 more to 10 more
elements.reason: Interval type (Credible Interval) is reported, but the specific calculation method is not explicitly detailed.

elements.quote: three Markov chains with 100 000 iterations after an initial burn-in of 10 000 and a thinning of 10.
elements.reason: Implementation details (chains, iterations, burn-in, thinning) are reported.

elements.quote: Wechoseanon-informativepriorforthevarianceparameter and a uniform prior for the effect parameter.
elements.reason: Prior distributions for variance and effect parameters are described.
No mention of methods used to account for statistical dependency among multiple estimates from the same study.

elements.quote: different prophylactic drugs were assessed precluding meta-analysis. Further, neither trial met the sample size criteria for network meta-analysis.
elements.reason: Planned syntheses judged impossible are identified with reasons (different drugs, sample size).

elements.reason: The text lists the specific factors and criteria considered for rating certainty.

elements.quote: Criteria for rating the certainty for each comparison and outcome as high, moderate, low, or very low, included considerations of risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, publication bias, intransitivity, incoherence, and imprecision.
